▶ WHAT IS ON THE BRANCH — three commits, each with a two-canon reducer:
 (1) ec5f6eed6 fix(mir): _MIR_builtin_func ADOPTS an existing import of the same name.
     THE LAST SELF-HOSTING BLOCKER, and the fix direction UPDATE 76 banked was WRONG. It is NOT a context problem: madc already calls a fresh MIR_init() per compile, and c2m's two-tier main_ctx/per-thread model (c2mir-driver.c:723/803/854, MIR_change_module_ctx) is for compiler THREADS, not this. It is NOT the resolver being name-blind either: c2m's object_import_resolver is character-for-character identical to madc's, sentinel and all — I tried declining MIR-reserved names there and it only traded the error for "import of undefined item mir.arg_memcpy", because MIR_link demands a non-NULL resolution.
     THE REAL ASYMMETRY: c2mir parses an asm label into an N_ASM node and DISCARDS it (c2mir.c:4527), so its reference keeps the ORIGINAL identifier and the two names never meet. madc implements asm labels faithfully (Program::consume_gnu_asm_label -> emit_symbol), as gcc does, so in mir-debug.c the name `mir.arg_memcpy` is BOTH an import the program spells (line 2556) and the helper the generator registers (mir-gen-x86_64.c:548). MIR_link bound it first; _MIR_builtin_func then refused it. The registrar now adopts an existing IMPORT item and repoints the module's own import at it; a non-import item of that name is still a real conflict and still raises. Proof both ways: renaming the asm label in a copy of mir-debug.c made it compile, and a struct too small to travel as a MIR block argument never registers the helper. c2m's object carries BOTH `U mir.arg_memcpy` and `U probe`, which is the direct evidence it dropped the label. UPSTREAM BUG — worth a PR after master.
 (2) 4ee5a601c fix(lexer): a type QUALIFIER may sit inside a specifier run. C99 6.7.2p2 — `unsigned const char` is the same type as `const unsigned char`. The lexer's chibicc-style bitmap accumulator ended its run at the first non-type-specifier word, so the lone `unsigned` minted as `unsigned int` and `const char` arrived as a SECOND base type. It now reads past an interleaved qualifier and hands it back AFTER the minted type token (the trailing-qualifier spelling, which the parser already accepted — that is why `unsigned char const *` always worked and the failure looked arbitrary). _pushback PREPENDS, so pushing the qualifiers last puts them ahead of whatever the loop already gave back.
 (3) b779baf91 test(lane): index-c — the new corpus, see below.

▶ THE NEW LANE — index-c, registered GATED in the fast tier (scripts/index_c_lane.sh + fast_lanes.sh). kostya/index-c (MIT), one self-contained 16k-line C program, ~50 real-world tasks. It VERIFIES ITSELF: every task computes a checksum against a known-expected value and the program exit(1)s if any fails, so a wrong lowering surfaces as a WRONG ANSWER, not a crash — the silent-wrong-answer class the .expect suites are weakest at. Corpus is cloned on the container at /workspace/index-c and RUN IN PLACE (never vendored), like the gcc testsuites. Lane runs -O2 because it is both faster AND stricter. Measured, all 50/50 correct in every configuration:
       gcc -O0 118.0s | madc default 104.0s (madc 0.88x — FASTER than gcc -O0)
       gcc -O2  54.2s | madc -O2      85.0s (madc 1.57x)
       gcc -O3  51.8s | madc -O3      85.2s (identical to its own -O2: MIR's gen tops out at level 2)
     gcc gains 2.2x from -O0 to -O2, madc 1.2x. That gap IS the optimizer gap and this lane now measures it. Lane wall time ~111s.
     ⚠️ -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE is REQUIRED and is NOT a workaround: `gcc -std=c17` fails on the same two CLOCK_MONOTONIC/CLOCK_REALTIME lines. It becomes --std=gnu* when that lands.

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
